findings.title: `source_bar_stamping` is the only enum field without an exact-type runtime guard
findings.description:
`Market.__post_init__` validates `source_bar_stamping` with `if self.source_bar_stamping not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` (a `frozenset` of `TimeMeaning` members, `markets.py:48-50`), while every other enum field in the same module goes through `_require_instance` — `session_mode` at `markets.py:64-66`, `continuity_kind` at `markets.py:102-104`, each calendar ref at `markets.py:146`, each basis at `markets.py:165`. The `_require_instance` helper's own comment at `markets.py:133` states the policy: "Runtime guard: callers may pass values the static types forbid." `test_markets.py:113-125` explicitly asserts a plain `"regular"` string is rejected for `session_mode`, but `test_markets.py:121-122` only tries `AVAILABLE_AT`/`EVENT_TIME` enum members for stamping; no test covers a plain `"period_start"`.

`StrEnum` members compare equal to their values, and since `str.__hash__` precedes `Enum.__hash__` in the MRO, they hash like their values too. So `Market(..., source_bar_stamping="period_start", ...)` passes the membership test and stores a plain `str` in a field declared `TimeMeaning`. `canonical.py:194-201` then encodes it via `_encode_str` rather than `_encode_enum`; the bytes happen to match, so identity does not drift, but any consumer doing an identity/enum check (as `test_markets.py:161` does with `is meaning`, and as 140's availability logic is expected to) silently takes the wrong branch. The same looseness extends to `calendar_id_for` (`markets.py:106-113`), where `ref.session_mode == mode` also accepts a plain string. Add `_require_instance(self.source_bar_stamping, TimeMeaning, "market.source_bar_stamping")` plus a rejection row to `REJECTED_MARKETS`, and consider guarding the lookup parameters.

findings.title: `Market`'s declared field types reject the iterables its docstring and tests promise
findings.description: The `Market` docstring (`markets.py:74-75`) says "`session_calendars` and `adjustment_bases` accept any iterable and are stored normalized", and the design's Implementation Details repeat "Market accepts any iterable for `session_calendars` and `adjustment_bases`". But the dataclass fields are annotated `tuple[SessionCalendarRef, ...]` and `frozenset[AdjustmentBasis]` (`markets.py:83,85`); only the private normalizers accept `Iterable` (`markets.py:143-144, 160-161`). `test_markets.py:151-156` and `test_markets.py:38-47` pass a generator, a `set` and `list`s — but only by unpacking a `dict[str, Any]`, which hides the mismatch from pyright. `pyproject.toml` sets `typeCheckingMode = "strict"` and CI (`ci.yml`) gates `uv run pyright`, so any statically typed caller (e.g. slice 140's metadata adapter building a `Market` from a list) gets `reportArgumentType` despite following the documented contract. Either type the constructor parameters as `Iterable` via an explicit `__init__` (keeping the stored attributes as tuple/frozenset), or change the docstring/design to state that callers must pass normalized values. Note `_normalize_bases` also builds `frozenset(bases)` before validating elements (`markets.py:161-165`), so a non-iterable or unhashable value from a dynamic caller escapes as a bare `TypeError` instead of the documented `InvalidMarketError`.

findings.title: Unused `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS` constant in the uniformity test
findings.description: `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS = 60_000_000_000` is defined but never referenced: `UNIFORM_ROWS` (`test_market_uniformity.py:36-42`) hardcodes each expected end as a hand-written literal, and a repository-wide grep finds no other use of the name. The literals are intentional per the task breakdown ("expected end is the start plus 60 seconds as a literal"), so the constant is dead code that also leaves the 60-second bar width defined in two competing places. Delete it, or use it to derive the expected ends if the hand-written-oracle requirement is relaxed.
